name: Audio-Visual Delay
mechanism:
This method analyzes 動画 frames for deepfake and AI generation detection:

1. **Frame Extraction**: Key frames are extracted from the 動画 stream for analysis.

2. **Feature Analysis**: Measures audio-動画 synchronization delay. Relevant visual and temporal features are computed per frame.

3. **Temporal Consistency Check**: Features are tracked across consecutive frames to detect inconsistencies.

4. **Pattern Matching**: Results are compared against known deepfake artifact patterns.

5. **スコア計算**: A confidence score (0-100) reflecting the likelihood of AI manipulation is calculated.
parameters:
分析タイプ: sensor
メディア: 動画
入力: Video frames extracted at key intervals
出力: 信頼度スコア (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: 中〜高 — 70-88% 単独精度. Most effective when combined with other 動画 forensic methods. Performance depends on 動画 quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated 動画 through audio-visual delay analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for 動画 authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard 動画 formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other 動画 forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by 動画 compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic 動画

references.title: Chugh, K. et al. (2020). Not Made for Each Other — Audio-Visual Dissonance-based Deepfake Detection. ACM MM.
Mittal, T. et al. (2020). Emotions Don't Lie: An Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection Method Using Affective Cues. ACM MM.
